67: - **Peligro Ambiental:** Esporas venenosas y flora carnívora
68: - **Ecología / Enemigos:** Hongos titánicos, bestias de la sombra, depredadores miméticos
69: - **Recursos Clave:** Madera férrea, veneno concentrado, seda umbría
70: 
71: ### Mapa 4.1: Bosque de Cristales Abisales (Tier 4: El Abismo Corrompido (Nv. 46-55))
72: - **Peligro Ambiental:** Radiación arcana y reflejos cegadores
73: - **Ecología / Enemigos:** Gólems arcanos, merodeadores de energía, cristálidos
74: - **Recursos Clave:** Cristal abisal, mithril corrupto, esencia pura
75: 
76: ### Mapa 4.2: Ciénagas de Sangre Estancada (Tier 4: El Abismo Corrompido (Nv. 46-55))
77: - **Peligro Ambiental:** Corrupción hemática continua
78: - **Ecología / Enemigos:** Mutaciones biológicas, horrores con tentáculos, inquisidores oscuros
79: - **Recursos Clave:** Icor abisal, cuero mutado, hierba carmesí
80: 
81: ### Mapa 4.3: Meseta de los Titanes Caídos (Tier 4: El Abismo Corrompido (Nv. 46-55))
82: - **Peligro Ambiental:** Tormentas eléctricas estáticas
83: - **Ecología / Enemigos:** Colosos rotos, elementales de tormenta, vigilantes celestes
84: - **Recursos Clave:** Metal estelar, núcleos de rayo, piedra rúnica
85: 
86: ### Mapa 5.1: Pasillos del Vacío Mecánico (Tier 5: Núcleo de los Arquitectos (Nv. 56-60))
87: - **Peligro Ambiental:** Trampas láser y drenaje de maná
88: - **Ecología / Enemigos:** Slime del Vacío, centinelas arquitectos, androides corruptos
89: - **Recursos Clave:** Aleación de arquitecto, condensadores arcanos
90: 
91: ### Mapa 5.2: El Abismo Espejado (Tier 5: Núcleo de los Arquitectos (Nv. 56-60))
92: - **Peligro Ambiental:** Gravedad alterada e ilusiones
93: - **Ecología / Enemigos:** Constructos cuánticos, entidades incorpóreas, reflejos oscuros
94: - **Recursos Clave:** Fragmentos dimensionales, tela etérea
95: 
96: ### Mapa 5.3: La Cámara del Eclipse (Tier 5: Núcleo de los Arquitectos (Nv. 56-60))
97: - **Peligro Ambiental:** Densidad máxima de Niebla Cenicienta
98: - **Ecología / Enemigos:** Horrores primordiales y el Avatar de la Niebla (Jefe Final)
99: - **Recursos Clave:** Núcleos primordiales y planos legendarios
100: 
101: ## 4. ECOLOGÍA DE ENEMIGOS (90 VARIEDADES) Y JERARQUÍA DE COMBATE
102: - **Variantes Inteligentes (~35% del Bestiario):** Familias evolutivas que escalan mecánicamente por Tier (ej. Slime Común -> Slime de Ácido -> Slime de Hielo -> Slime de Magma -> Slime del Vacío; y familias de bandidos/cultistas).
103: - **Criaturas Exclusivas por Bioma (~55% del Bestiario):** Monstruos endémicos que jamás se repiten fuera de su mapa natal (yetis, vermes de arena, constructos cuánticos, horrores hemáticos).
104: - **Jerarquía de Amenazas:**
105:   1. **Enemigos Comunes (Mobs):** Patrullas de 2 a 4 criaturas.
106:   2. **Enemigos Raros:** Prefijos aleatorios de afijos (*Voraz, Espectral, Blindado, Veloz*), doble XP y materiales raros.
107:   3. **Élites de Zona:** Minijefes fijos en puntos estratégicos y entradas de mazmorras.
108:   4. **Jefes de Mazmorra e Incursión (Bosses):** Fases múltiples, invocaciones y ataques en área telegráficos.
109: 
110: ## 5. ESCALA DE CALIDADES Y RAREZAS DE ÍTEMS
111: - **Común (Blanco):** 0 afijos | Huecos de Runa: 0 | Función: Reciclaje en materiales básicos de herrería y peletería.
112: - **Inusual (Verde):** 1 afijo menor | Huecos de Runa: 0 | Función: Bonificaciones iniciales de probabilidad crítica o recolección.
113: - **Raro (Azul):** 2 a 3 afijos | Huecos de Runa: 1 | Función: Equipo sólido de progresión media con 1 hueco de runa.
114: - **Épico (Morado):** 3 afijos mayores | Huecos de Runa: 2 | Función: Atributos base altos; exclusivo de Élites, Jefes y mazmorras profundas.
115: - **Legendario (Naranja):** 3 afijos + Poder Único | Huecos de Runa: 2 | Función: Modifica mecánicamente las habilidades de tu clase híbrida.
116: 
117: ## 6. SUPERVIVENCIA, CLIMA, CICLO DÍA/NOCHE Y MAZMORRAS
118: - **Ciclo Día/Noche:** De noche aumentan el rango de agresión y el daño de los monstruos, pero emergen plantas y menas nocturnas exclusivas.
119: - **Clima Extremo:** Hipotermia en Tundra y deshidratación/calor extremo en el Desierto de Ceniza; requieren armaduras térmicas de Peletería y comidas de Cocina.
120: - **Mazmorras Dinámicas:** De 3 a 5 niveles de profundidad procedural con oscuridad creciente, trampas mecánicas (placas de presión, dardos, fosos) y botines abisales exclusivos.
121: 
122: ## 7. SISTEMA DE RECOLECCIÓN (6) Y CRAFTEO CRUZADO (5)
123: - **6 Profesiones de Recolección:** Minería, Tala, Desuello (Skinning), Pesca, Herboristería y Tejeduría de Telas (todas exigen herramientas con durabilidad y Tier acorde).
124: - **5 Profesiones de Manufactura Interdependiente:** Herrería, Peletería, Alquimia, Encantamiento y Cocina.
125: 
126: ## 8. MATRIZ MAESTRA DE LAS 16 CLASES HÍBRIDAS (4 x 4)
127: Todos inician como *Aldeano* (Nv. 1-14). Al Nv. 15 eligen Clase Primaria y al Nv. 30 Subclase:
128: 
129: 1. **Arquero + Inquebrantable** (Tirador pesado de posición fija y alta resistencia física.)
130:    - *Activas:* Disparo de Anclaje, Baluarte de Ballestero
131:    - *Pasivas:* Postura Firme, Armadura de Campaña
132: 2. **Arquero + Elementista** (Control elemental a distancia y manipulación de proyectiles.)
133:    - *Activas:* Flecha Elemental Adaptativa, Muro de Viento
134:    - *Pasivas:* Corriente Residual, Balística Dinámica
135: 3. **Arquero + Clérigo** (Daño radiante contra corrupción y soporte de grupo/supervivencia.)
136:    - *Activas:* Saeta de Juicio Divino, Aura de Purificación Menor
137:    - *Pasivas:* Bendición del Tirador, Fervor de la Fe
138: 4. **Arquero + Potenciador** (Especialista táctico en trampas, venenos y explosivos alquímicos.)
139:    - *Activas:* Trampa de Abrojos Cinéticos, Tintura de Precisión
140:    - *Pasivas:* Ojo de Halcón Concentrado, Catálisis de Trampas
141: 5. **Mago + Inquebrantable** (Mago de batalla blindado capaz de resistir embates cuerpo a cuerpo.)
142:    - *Activas:* Pulso de Hierro Arcano, Escudo de Placas Mágicas
143:    - *Pasivas:* Absorción de Impacto, Resistencia Pesada Innata
144: 6. **Mago + Elementista** (Destrucción elemental masiva en área con reacciones combinadas.)
145:    - *Activas:* Tormenta Convergente, Escudo de Prisma
146:    - *Pasivas:* Catálisis Instintiva, Sintonía de Leyes Físicas
147: 7. **Mago + Clérigo** (Canalizador arcano-sagrado con regeneración y zonas de protección.)
148:    - *Activas:* Nova Sagrada, Santuario de Maná
149:    - *Pasivas:* Gracia Divina, Sinergia de Fe
150: 8. **Mago + Potenciador** (Amplificador de consumibles, runas y daño explosivo de catalizadores.)
151:    - *Activas:* Sobrecarga Catalítica, Campo de Infusión
152:    - *Pasivas:* Maestría de Reactivos, Resonancia de Polvo Arcano
153: 9. **Guerrero + Inquebrantable** (Duelista implacable que convierte el daño mitigado en contraataques.)
154:    - *Activas:* Baluarte Titánico, Estocada de Acero Vengativa
155:    - *Pasivas:* Voluntad de Hierro, Absolución de Daño
156: 10. **Guerrero + Elementista** (Espadachín elemental que infunde sus armas con fuego, hielo o rayo.)
157:    - *Activas:* Corte de Hoja Rúnica, Imbuir Armadura Elemental
158:    - *Pasivas:* Furia Elemental, Conducción de Calor
159: 11. **Guerrero + Clérigo** (Paladín ofensivo de primera línea con robo de vida sagrado.)
160:    - *Activas:* Golpe de Venganza Sagrada, Aura de Devoción
161:    - *Pasivas:* Martirio Justiciero, Resiliencia Bendita
162: 12. **Guerrero + Potenciador** (Berserker alquímico de daño físico bruto y ruptura de defensas.)
163:    - *Activas:* Inyección de Furia, Golpe Sísmico Rompe-Armaduras
164:    - *Pasivas:* Adrenalina Pura, Filo Afilado
165: 13. **Tanque + Inquebrantable** (Fortaleza viviente con control de masas y mitigación máxima.)
166:    - *Activas:* Carga de Embestida Sísmica, Provocación de Hierro Forjado
167:    - *Pasivas:* Muro de Escudos Inquebrantable, Resiliencia de Armadura
168: 14. **Tanque + Elementista** (Guardián elemental que refleja daño térmico y ralentiza enemigos.)
169:    - *Activas:* Pisar de Magma Caliente, Baluarte de Escarcha
170:    - *Pasivas:* Aura Térmica Defensiva, Coraza Refractaria
171: 15. **Tanque + Clérigo** (Protector consagrado inmune a estados alterados de la Niebla.)
172:    - *Activas:* Aura de Tierra Santa, Intervención Divina
173:    - *Pasivas:* Fervor Sagrado, Sacrificio Protector
174: 16. **Tanque + Potenciador** (Comandante táctico que optimiza bufs de comida, pociones y área.)
175:    - *Activas:* Estandarte de Resistencia, Carga de Catalizador Explosivo
176:    - *Pasivas:* Maestría de Posicionamiento, Logística de Supervivencia
177: 
178: ## 9. COMBATE EN TIEMPO REAL, CONTROLES TÁCTILES Y HUD MINIMALISTA
179: - **Dual-Stick Flotante:** Joystick izquierdo dinámico de movimiento; botón grande de ataque básico a la derecha, matriz compacta 2x2 para las habilidades activas de subclase y botón contextual de interacción/recolección.
180: - **Gestión de Estamina:** Correr, rodar/esquivar y ataques cargados consumen estamina; agotarla provoca estado de *Exhausto*.
181: - **HUD Minimalista:** Barras de vida, maná y estamina dinámicas que se atenúan fuera de combate para maximizar la visibilidad en pantallas móviles.
182: 
183: ## 10. ECONOMÍA, REFUGIO PERSONAL, PUERTO OCASO Y MUERTE (CORPSE RUN)
184: - **Economía Restrictiva:** El oro es escaso; reparar equipo dañado cuesta oro creciente según el Tier.
185: - **Refugio Personal (4 Fases):** Campamento Roto -> Cabaña de Troncos -> Mansión de Piedra -> Ciudadela. Incluye **Banco Seguro** para guardar oro y materiales a salvo de la muerte.
186: - **Castigo por Muerte y Redención:** Al morir pierdes un % de XP actual, la durabilidad del equipo cae drásticamente y dejas una Mochila/Lápida con el 80% de tu inventario en el lugar de tu muerte para intentar rescatarla.

## Objective
- Build and validate a playable, Android-friendly browser survival ARPG based on *Wild Frontier — La Frontera Maldita*.
- Compare implementation with the GDD and report coverage, gaps, assumptions, and landscape/portrait guidance.

## Requirements
- Implement mobile-first gameplay with 15 maps, 90 enemies, 16 hybrid classes, gathering and crafting, survival systems, shelter, and corpse-run recovery.
- Preserve harsh progression and loss/recovery systems; briefly note assumptions when finished.

## Decisions
- Use a browser-based game shell.

## Work State
### Completed
- Preliminary game shell and systems exist; `xpFill` lookup and GDD-aligned gathering/crafting profession names were added.
- Confirmed definitions for 15 maps, 90 generated enemy entries, and 16 hybrid classes.
- Inspected relevant gameplay, save/load, controls, crafting, corpse handling, and GDD sections; outstanding issues remain as listed below.

### Active
- Fix progression and class selection: start as Aldeano, unlock primary class at level 15 and subclass at level 30, and preserve character progress when selecting.
- Fix joystick pointer tracking and show the orientation prompt after viewport changes.
- Gate map access by player level/tier and reject invalid map indices.
- Implement meaningful crafting effects and correct recipe costs.
- Persist corpse state across saves/maps and make death inventory loss match the 80% non-bank loot rule.
- Validate gameplay, browser console, and screenshot; compare implementation against the GDD and report coverage, gaps, assumptions, and orientation guidance.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement class progression and selection without replacing/resetting the player.
2. Address joystick, orientation, map access, crafting, and corpse loss/persistence issues.
3. Run browser/gameplay checks and compare the result with the GDD.

## Relevant Files
- `js/main.js`: gameplay systems, maps/classes, save/load, controls, crafting, and corpse handling.
- `index.html`: HUD and game shell markup.
- `styles.css`: mobile-first layout and controls.
- `/tmp/gdd/01_GDD_MAESTRO_COMPLETO.md`: full design requirements and progression rules.
- `/tmp/gdd/04_GDD_DATA_STRUCTURES.json`: structured map and class definitions.
- `/tmp/opencode/wild-frontier.png`: prior browser screenshot.
- `/tmp/opencode/chromium.log`: prior Chromium output.

## Important Context
- Project files are uncommitted and untracked.
- `createPlayer()` applies class-derived stats while labeling the character Aldeano; it sets `primaryClassId` and `subclassId` to `null`. Class-sheet selection replaces the player entirely.
- `createMap()` wraps map indices and clears `state.corpse`; `loadGame()` recreates the map without restoring corpse state; `renderMapSheet()` currently allows every map.
- Crafting has six recipes; only three have distinct effects, `Pechera de cuero` requires undefined `hilo`, and other recipes report generic success.
- Death randomly assigns inventory to the corpse despite the message claiming 80% of non-bank loot is stored.
- Joystick handling relies on `:active` and element-level release/leave events; the orientation prompt is only checked during initial setup.
- A local server previously returned HTTP 200 at `http://127.0.0.1:8765`; Chromium is available, but Playwright and Puppeteer are not.

10: ## 1. FILOSOFÍA DE DISEÑO Y PROGRESIÓN DURA
11: - **La Regla de Oro:** La habilidad mecánica de combate no basta; la inteligencia logística y la preparación previa son obligatorias. Los enemigos escalan con una curva empinada y las estadísticas base del personaje se estancan rápido si no se mejora el equipo mediante crafteo.
12: - **Interdependencia Crítica:** Entrar a una mazmorra de Tier alto sin pociones de alquimia, sin equipo reparado al 100% o sin alimentos cocinados de larga duración garantiza la derrota.
13: - **Progresión Orgánica:** Subir de nivel otorga puntos de atributo base y acceso a clases (Nv. 15) y subclases (Nv. 30), pero el verdadero poder proviene del Tier del equipo, las runas de encantamiento y las mejoras del Refugio Personal.
14: 
15: ## 2. LORE, HISTORIA Y ESTRUCTURA DE CAMPAÑA ("LA FRONTERA MALDITA")
16: - **El Lore:** La Gran Flota de Expedición imperial naufragó en las costas de **Aethelgard**, un continente virgen corrompido por la *Niebla Cenicienta*. Cada muerte sin rescate de cadáver alimenta la maldición del entorno. Los supervivientes se agrupan en el bastión de **Puerto Ocaso**.
17: - **Estructura de Campaña por Actos:**
18:   - **Acto I (Tier 1 | Niveles 1-15):** Playas, Praderas y Bosques Bajos. Supervivencia básica, recolección inicial y construcción del refugio de troncos.
19:   - **Acto II (Tier 2 | Niveles 16-30):** Pantanos Ácidos, Cañones y Ruinas Superiores. Elección de Clase Primaria y Subclase. Exigencia de alquimia defensiva.
20:   - **Acto III (Tier 3 | Niveles 31-45):** Tundra Eterna, Desierto Volcánico y Jungla Umbría. Clima extremo letal y recolección especializada.
21:   - **Acto IV (Tiers 4-5 | Niveles 46-60):** El Abismo Corrompido y el Núcleo de los Arquitectos hasta la Cámara del Eclipse.
22:

101: ## 4. ECOLOGÍA DE ENEMIGOS (90 VARIEDADES) Y JERARQUÍA DE COMBATE
102: - **Variantes Inteligentes (~35% del Bestiario):** Familias evolutivas que escalan mecánicamente por Tier (ej. Slime Común -> Slime de Ácido -> Slime de Hielo -> Slime de Magma -> Slime del Vacío; y familias de bandidos/cultistas).
103: - **Criaturas Exclusivas por Bioma (~55% del Bestiario):** Monstruos endémicos que jamás se repiten fuera de su mapa natal (yetis, vermes de arena, constructos cuánticos, horrores hemáticos).
104: - **Jerarquía de Amenazas:**
105:   1. **Enemigos Comunes (Mobs):** Patrullas de 2 a 4 criaturas.
106:   2. **Enemigos Raros:** Prefijos aleatorios de afijos (*Voraz, Espectral, Blindado, Veloz*), doble XP y materiales raros.
107:   3. **Élites de Zona:** Minijefes fijos en puntos estratégicos y entradas de mazmorras.
108:   4. **Jefes de Mazmorra e Incursión (Bosses):** Fases múltiples, invocaciones y ataques en área telegráficos.
109: 
110: ## 5. ESCALA DE CALIDADES Y RAREZAS DE ÍTEMS
111: - **Común (Blanco):** 0 afijos | Huecos de Runa: 0 | Función: Reciclaje en materiales básicos de herrería y peletería.
112: - **Inusual (Verde):** 1 afijo menor | Huecos de Runa: 0 | Función: Bonificaciones iniciales de probabilidad crítica o recolección.
113: - **Raro (Azul):** 2 a 3 afijos | Huecos de Runa: 1 | Función: Equipo sólido de progresión media con 1 hueco de runa.
114: - **Épico (Morado):** 3 afijos mayores | Huecos de Runa: 2 | Función: Atributos base altos; exclusivo de Élites, Jefes y mazmorras profundas.
115: - **Legendario (Naranja):** 3 afijos + Poder Único | Huecos de Runa: 2 | Función: Modifica mecánicamente las habilidades de tu clase híbrida.
116: 
117: ## 6. SUPERVIVENCIA, CLIMA, CICLO DÍA/NOCHE Y MAZMORRAS
118: - **Ciclo Día/Noche:** De noche aumentan el rango de agresión y el daño de los monstruos, pero emergen plantas y menas nocturnas exclusivas.
119: - **Clima Extremo:** Hipotermia en Tundra y deshidratación/calor extremo en el Desierto de Ceniza; requieren armaduras térmicas de Peletería y comidas de Cocina.
120: - **Mazmorras Dinámicas:** De 3 a 5 niveles de profundidad procedural con oscuridad creciente, trampas mecánicas (placas de presión, dardos, fosos) y botines abisales exclusivos.

122: ## 7. SISTEMA DE RECOLECCIÓN (6) Y CRAFTEO CRUZADO (5)
123: - **6 Profesiones de Recolección:** Minería, Tala, Desuello (Skinning), Pesca, Herboristería y Tejeduría de Telas (todas exigen herramientas con durabilidad y Tier acorde).
124: - **5 Profesiones de Manufactura Interdependiente:** Herrería, Peletería, Alquimia, Encantamiento y Cocina.
125: 
126: ## 8. MATRIZ MAESTRA DE LAS 16 CLASES HÍBRIDAS (4 x 4)
127: Todos inician como *Aldeano* (Nv. 1-14). Al Nv. 15 eligen Clase Primaria y al Nv. 30 Subclase:

## Objective
- Build and validate a playable, Android-friendly browser survival ARPG based on *Wild Frontier — La Frontera Maldita*.
- Compare implementation against the GDD and report coverage, gaps, assumptions, and landscape/portrait guidance.

## Requirements
- Implement mobile-first gameplay with 15 maps, 90 enemies, 16 hybrid classes, gathering and crafting, survival systems, shelter, and corpse-run recovery.
- Preserve harsh progression and loss/recovery systems; briefly note assumptions when finished.

## Decisions
- Use a browser-based game shell.

## Work State
### Completed
- Preliminary game shell and systems exist; `xpFill` lookup and GDD-aligned gathering/crafting profession names were added.
- Confirmed definitions for 15 maps, 90 generated enemy entries, and 16 hybrid classes.
- Inspected gameplay, save/load, controls, crafting, corpse handling, and relevant GDD sections; identified outstanding issues.

### Active
- Fix progression and class selection: start as Aldeano, unlock primary class at level 15 and subclass at level 30, and preserve character progress when selecting.
- Fix joystick pointer tracking and show the orientation prompt after viewport changes.
- Gate map access by player level/tier and reject invalid map indices.
- Implement meaningful crafting effects and correct recipe costs.
- Persist corpse state across saves/maps and make death inventory loss match the 80% non-bank loot rule.
- Validate gameplay, browser console, and screenshot; compare implementation against the GDD and report coverage, gaps, assumptions, and orientation guidance.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement class progression and selection without replacing/resetting the player.
2. Address joystick, orientation, map access, crafting, and corpse loss/persistence issues.
3. Run browser/gameplay checks and compare the result against the GDD.

## Relevant Files
- `js/main.js`: gameplay systems, maps/classes, save/load, controls, crafting, and corpse handling.
- `index.html`: HUD and game shell markup.
- `styles.css`: mobile-first layout and controls.
- `/tmp/gdd/01_GDD_MAESTRO_COMPLETO.md`: full design requirements and progression rules.
- `/tmp/gdd/04_GDD_DATA_STRUCTURES.json`: structured map and class definitions.
- `/tmp/opencode/wild-frontier.png`: prior browser screenshot.
- `/tmp/opencode/chromium.log`: prior Chromium output.

## Important Context
- Project files are uncommitted and untracked.
- `createPlayer()` applies class-derived stats while labeling the character Aldeano; it sets `primaryClassId` and `subclassId` to `null`. Class-sheet selection replaces the player entirely.
- `createMap()` wraps map indices and clears `state.corpse`; `loadGame()` recreates the map without restoring corpse state; `renderMapSheet()` currently allows every map.
- Crafting has six recipes; only three have distinct effects, `Pechera de cuero` requires undefined `hilo`, and other recipes report generic success.
- Death randomly assigns inventory to the corpse despite the message claiming 80% of non-bank loot is stored.
- Joystick handling relies on `:active` and element-level release/leave events; the orientation prompt is only checked during initial setup.
- A local server previously returned HTTP 200 at `http://127.0.0.1:8765`; Chromium is available, but Playwright and Puppeteer are not.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build and validate a playable, Android-friendly browser survival ARPG based on *Wild Frontier — La Frontera Maldita*.
- Compare implementation against the GDD and report coverage, gaps, assumptions, and landscape/portrait guidance.

## Requirements
- Implement mobile-first gameplay with 15 maps, 90 enemies, 16 hybrid classes, gathering and crafting, survival systems, shelter, and corpse-run recovery.
- Preserve harsh progression and loss/recovery systems; briefly note assumptions when finished.

## Decisions
- Use a browser-based game shell.

## Work State
### Completed
- Preliminary game shell and systems exist; `xpFill` lookup and GDD-aligned gathering/crafting profession names were added.
- Confirmed definitions for 15 maps, 90 generated enemy entries, and 16 hybrid classes.
- Inspected gameplay, save/load, controls, crafting, corpse handling, and relevant GDD sections; identified outstanding issues.

### Active
- Fix progression and class selection: start as Aldeano, unlock primary class at level 15 and subclass at level 30, and preserve character progress when selecting.
- Fix joystick pointer tracking and show the orientation prompt after viewport changes.
- Gate map access by player level/tier and reject invalid map indices.
- Implement meaningful crafting effects and correct recipe costs.
- Persist corpse state across saves/maps and make death inventory loss match the 80% non-bank loot rule.
- Validate gameplay, browser console, and screenshot; compare implementation against the GDD and report coverage, gaps, assumptions, and orientation guidance.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement class progression and selection without replacing/resetting the player.
2. Address joystick, orientation, map access, crafting, and corpse loss/persistence issues.
3. Run browser/gameplay checks and compare the result against the GDD.

## Relevant Files
- `js/main.js`: gameplay systems, maps/classes, save/load, controls, crafting, and corpse handling.
- `index.html`: HUD and game shell markup.
- `styles.css`: mobile-first layout and controls.

1: # GAME DESIGN DOCUMENT (GDD) MAESTRO Y EXTENSO
2: ## PROJECT: WILD FRONTIER — LA FRONTERA MALDITA
3: 
4: - **Género:** ARPG de Supervivencia 2D / Sandbox de Exploración, Crafteo y Progresión Hardcore.
5: - **Plataforma:** Android (Optimizado para pantallas táctiles, HUD minimalista, rendimiento fluido en motores 2D como Godot 4 o Unity URP).
6: - **Enfoque de Diseño:** Dificultad implacable, progresión lenta y deliberada, interdependencia estricta de sistemas logísticos, economía restrictiva y castigos severos por muerte con opción de redención táctica (Corpse Run).
7: 
8: ---
9: 
10: ## 1. FILOSOFÍA DE DISEÑO Y PROGRESIÓN DURA
11: - **La Regla de Oro:** La habilidad mecánica de combate no basta; la inteligencia logística y la preparación previa son obligatorias. Los enemigos escalan con una curva empinada y las estadísticas base del personaje se estancan rápido si no se mejora el equipo mediante crafteo.
12: - **Interdependencia Crítica:** Entrar a una mazmorra de Tier alto sin pociones de alquimia, sin equipo reparado al 100% o sin alimentos cocinados de larga duración garantiza la derrota.
13: - **Progresión Orgánica:** Subir de nivel otorga puntos de atributo base y acceso a clases (Nv. 15) y subclases (Nv. 30), pero el verdadero poder proviene del Tier del equipo, las runas de encantamiento y las mejoras del Refugio Personal.
14: 
15: ## 2. LORE, HISTORIA Y ESTRUCTURA DE CAMPAÑA ("LA FRONTERA MALDITA")
16: - **El Lore:** La Gran Flota de Expedición imperial naufragó en las costas de **Aethelgard**, un continente virgen corrompido por la *Niebla Cenicienta*. Cada muerte sin rescate de cadáver alimenta la maldición del entorno. Los supervivientes se agrupan en el bastión de **Puerto Ocaso**.
17: - **Estructura de Campaña por Actos:**
18:   - **Acto I (Tier 1 | Niveles 1-15):** Playas, Praderas y Bosques Bajos. Supervivencia básica, recolección inicial y construcción del refugio de troncos.
19:   - **Acto II (Tier 2 | Niveles 16-30):** Pantanos Ácidos, Cañones y Ruinas Superiores. Elección de Clase Primaria y Subclase. Exigencia de alquimia defensiva.
20:   - **Acto III (Tier 3 | Niveles 31-45):** Tundra Eterna, Desierto Volcánico y Jungla Umbría. Clima extremo letal y recolección especializada.
21:   - **Acto IV (Tiers 4-5 | Niveles 46-60):** El Abismo Corrompido y el Núcleo de los Arquitectos hasta la Cámara del Eclipse.
22: 
23: ## 3. ARQUITECTURA DEL MUNDO: 15 MAPAS EXTENSOS (3 POR TIER)
24: Los mapas utilizan generación procedural por chunks para su distribución interna, manteniendo fija su identidad de bioma híbrida (sprites PNG artesanales + iluminación y clima por shaders):
25: 
26: ### Mapa 1.1: Playas del Náufrago (Tier 1: La Frontera Primitiva (Nv. 1-15))
27: - **Peligro Ambiental:** Mareas y emboscadas costeras
28: - **Ecología / Enemigos:** Cangrejos acorazados, bandidos novatos, slimes comunes
29: - **Recursos Clave:** Madera a la deriva, cobre superficial, peces costeros
30: 
31: ### Mapa 1.2: Praderas Susurrantes (Tier 1: La Frontera Primitiva (Nv. 1-15))
32: - **Peligro Ambiental:** Vientos dinámicos y manadas rápidas

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build and validate a playable, Android-friendly browser survival ARPG based on *Wild Frontier — La Frontera Maldita*.
- Compare implementation against the GDD and report coverage, gaps, assumptions, and landscape/portrait guidance.

## Requirements
- Implement mobile-first gameplay with 15 maps, 90 enemies, 16 hybrid classes, gathering and crafting, survival systems, shelter, and corpse-run recovery.
- Preserve harsh progression and loss/recovery systems; briefly note assumptions when finished.

## Decisions
- Use a browser-based game shell.

## Work State
### Completed
- Preliminary game shell and systems exist; `xpFill` lookup and GDD-aligned gathering/crafting profession names were added.
- Confirmed definitions for 15 maps, 90 generated enemy entries, and 16 hybrid classes.

### Active
- Finish class progression: begin as Aldeano, unlock primary class at level 15 and subclass at level 30; selection must preserve player progress.
- Fix joystick pointer tracking and show the orientation prompt after viewport changes.
- Gate map access by player level/tier and reject invalid map indices.
- Implement meaningful crafting effects and correct recipe costs.
- Persist corpse state across saves/maps and make death inventory loss match the 80% non-bank loot rule.
- Validate gameplay, browser console, and screenshot; compare implementation against the GDD and report coverage, gaps, assumptions, and orientation guidance.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue class selection work in `js/main.js`: the new `classIndex()` and `applyClassChoice()` helpers were added, but class-sheet wiring and level-gated choices remain.
2. Address remaining progression, joystick/orientation, map access, crafting, and corpse-loss/persistence issues.
3. Run browser/gameplay checks and compare the result against the GDD.

## Relevant Files
- `js/main.js`: gameplay systems, maps/classes, save/load, controls, crafting, and corpse handling.
- `index.html`: HUD and game shell markup.
- `styles.css`: mobile-first layout and controls.
- `/tmp/gdd/01_GDD_MAESTRO_COMPLETO.md`: full design requirements and progression rules.
- `/tmp/gdd/04_GDD_DATA_STRUCTURES.json`: structured map and class definitions.

## Important Context
- Project files are uncommitted and untracked.
- `createPlayer()` labels the character Aldeano but initializes stats using a class definition; class-sheet selection currently replaces the player.
- `applyClassChoice(primaryId, subclassId)` now validates level and class IDs, updates class fields/skills, applies basic primary-class stat bonuses on first selection, and saves; it is not yet connected to `renderClassSheet()`.
- `createMap()` wraps indices and clears `state.corpse`; `loadGame()` recreates the map without restoring corpse state; `renderMapSheet()` currently allows every map.
- Crafting has six recipes; only three have distinct effects, `Pechera de cuero` requires undefined `hilo`, and other recipes report generic success.
- Death randomly assigns inventory to the corpse despite the message claiming 80% of non-bank loot is stored.
- Joystick handling relies on `:active` and element-level release/leave events; the orientation prompt is only checked during initial setup.
- GDD specifies class selection at levels 15 and 30 and says the corpse holds 80% of inventory at the death location; the bank protects stored materials and gold.
- Local server previously returned HTTP 200 at `http://127.0.0.1:8765`; Chromium is available, but Playwright and Puppeteer are not.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build and validate a playable, Android-friendly browser survival ARPG based on *Wild Frontier — La Frontera Maldita*.
- Compare implementation against the GDD and report coverage, gaps, assumptions, and landscape/portrait guidance.

## Requirements
- Implement mobile-first gameplay with 15 maps, 90 enemies, 16 hybrid classes, gathering and crafting, survival systems, shelter, and corpse-run recovery.
- Preserve harsh progression and loss/recovery systems; briefly note assumptions when finished.

## Decisions
- Use a browser-based game shell.

## Work State
### Completed
- Preliminary game shell and systems exist; `xpFill` lookup and GDD-aligned gathering/crafting profession names were added.
- Confirmed definitions for 15 maps, 90 generated enemy entries, and 16 hybrid classes.
- Added `classIndex()` and `applyClassChoice()` helpers in `js/main.js`; class selection validates level and IDs, preserves progress, and applies primary-class bonuses once.

### Active
- Finish class progression: begin as Aldeano, unlock primary class at level 15 and subclass at level 30; connect choices to `renderClassSheet()`.
- Fix joystick pointer tracking and show the orientation prompt after viewport changes.
- Gate map access by player level/tier and reject invalid map indices.
- Implement meaningful crafting effects and correct recipe costs.
- Persist corpse state across saves/maps and make death inventory loss match the 80% non-bank loot rule.
- Validate gameplay, browser console, and screenshot; compare implementation against the GDD and report coverage, gaps, assumptions, and orientation guidance.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Wire `renderClassSheet()` to `applyClassChoice()` and enforce primary/subclass unlock rules without replacing the player.
2. Address remaining progression, joystick/orientation, map access, crafting, and corpse-loss/persistence issues.
3. Run browser/gameplay checks and compare the result against the GDD.

## Relevant Files
- `js/main.js`: gameplay systems, maps/classes, save/load, controls, crafting, and corpse handling.
- `index.html`: HUD and game shell markup.
- `styles.css`: mobile-first layout and controls.
- `/tmp/gdd/01_GDD_MAESTRO_COMPLETO.md`: full design requirements and progression rules.
- `/tmp/gdd/04_GDD_DATA_STRUCTURES.json`: structured map and class definitions.

## Important Context
- Project files are uncommitted and untracked.
- `applyClassChoice()` is not yet connected to `renderClassSheet()`; the current sheet still replaces the player on class selection.
- `createMap()` wraps indices and clears `state.corpse`; `loadGame()` recreates the map without restoring corpse state; `renderMapSheet()` currently allows every map.
- Crafting has six recipes; only three have distinct effects, `Pechera de cuero` requires undefined `hilo`, and other recipes report generic success.
- Death randomly assigns inventory to the corpse despite the message claiming 80% of non-bank loot is stored.
- Joystick handling relies on `:active` and element-level release/leave events; the orientation prompt is only checked during initial setup.
- GDD specifies class selection at levels 15 and 30 and says the corpse holds 80% of inventory at the death location; the bank protects stored materials and gold.
- Local server previously returned HTTP 200 at `http://127.0.0.1:8765`; Chromium is available, but Playwright and Puppeteer are not.

1: # GAME DESIGN DOCUMENT (GDD) MAESTRO Y EXTENSO
2: ## PROJECT: WILD FRONTIER — LA FRONTERA MALDITA
3: 
4: - **Género:** ARPG de Supervivencia 2D / Sandbox de Exploración, Crafteo y Progresión Hardcore.
5: - **Plataforma:** Android (Optimizado para pantallas táctiles, HUD minimalista, rendimiento fluido en motores 2D como Godot 4 o Unity URP).
6: - **Enfoque de Diseño:** Dificultad implacable, progresión lenta y deliberada, interdependencia estricta de sistemas logísticos, economía restrictiva y castigos severos por muerte con opción de redención táctica (Corpse Run).

## Objective
- Build and validate a playable, Android-friendly browser survival ARPG based on *Wild Frontier — La Frontera Maldita*.
- Compare implementation against the GDD and report coverage, gaps, assumptions, and landscape/portrait guidance.

## Requirements
- Implement mobile-first gameplay with 15 maps, 90 enemies, 16 hybrid classes, gathering and crafting, survival systems, shelter, and corpse-run recovery.
- Preserve harsh progression and loss/recovery systems; briefly note assumptions when finished.

## Decisions
- Use a browser-based game shell.

## Work State
### Completed
- Preliminary game shell and systems exist; `xpFill` lookup and GDD-aligned gathering/crafting profession names were added.
- Confirmed definitions for 15 maps, 90 generated enemy entries, and 16 hybrid classes.
- Added `classIndex()` and `applyClassChoice()` in `js/main.js`; class selection validates level and IDs, preserves progress, applies primary-class bonuses once, and retains the chosen subclass when updating a class.

### Active
- Wire `renderClassSheet()` to `applyClassChoice()` and enforce primary/subclass unlock rules without replacing the player.
- Fix joystick pointer tracking and show the orientation prompt after viewport changes.
- Gate map access by player level/tier and reject invalid map indices.
- Implement meaningful crafting effects and correct recipe costs.
- Persist corpse state across saves/maps and make death inventory loss match the 80% non-bank loot rule.
- Validate gameplay, browser console, and screenshot; compare implementation against the GDD and report coverage, gaps, assumptions, and orientation guidance.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Connect class-sheet choices to `applyClassChoice()` and present class choices according to level and selection state.
2. Address map access, joystick/orientation, crafting, and corpse loss/persistence.
3. Run browser/gameplay checks and compare the result against the GDD.

## Relevant Files
- `js/main.js`: gameplay systems, maps/classes, save/load, controls, crafting, and corpse handling.
- `index.html`: HUD and game shell markup.
- `styles.css`: mobile-first layout and controls.
- `/tmp/gdd/01_GDD_MAESTRO_COMPLETO.md`: full design requirements and progression rules.
- `/tmp/gdd/04_GDD_DATA_STRUCTURES.json`: structured map and class definitions.

## Important Context
- Project files are uncommitted and untracked.
- `renderClassSheet()` still replaces the player on class selection; the new helper is not connected yet.
- `createMap()` wraps indices and clears `state.corpse`; `loadGame()` recreates the map without restoring corpse state; `renderMapSheet()` currently allows every map.
- Crafting has six recipes; only three have distinct effects, `Pechera de cuero` requires undefined `hilo`, and other recipes report generic success.
- Death randomly assigns inventory to the corpse despite the message claiming 80% of non-bank loot is stored.
- Joystick handling relies on `:active` and element-level release/leave events; the orientation prompt is only checked during initial setup.
- GDD specifies class selection at levels 15 and 30 and says the corpse holds 80% of inventory at the death location; the bank protects stored materials and gold.
- Local server previously returned HTTP 200 at `http://127.0.0.1:8765`; Chromium is available, but Playwright and Puppeteer are not.

193: function buildEnemyLibrary() {

195:   const prefixes = ['Sombra', 'Tóxico', 'Cicatrizado', 'Lobo', 'Corrupto', 'Rápido', 'Ribereño', 'Gélido', 'Ferviente', 'Huesudo', 'Afilado', 'Mecánico', 'Eclipse', 'Mordedor', 'Ancestral', 'Orillero', 'Rúnico', 'Piloto', 'Umbral', 'Bárbaro'];

197:   for (let i = 0; i < 90; i += 1) {
198:     const base = i % 14;
199:     const variant = ['Cangrejo', 'Lobo', 'Esqueleto', 'Slime', 'Araña', 'Bandido', 'Jabalí', 'Goblin', 'Reptil', 'Treant', 'Mutante', 'Gólem', 'Yeti', 'Cultista'][base % 14];

804: function performAttack() {
805:   const p = state.player;
806:   if (!p || p.attackCooldown > 0) return;
807:   p.attackCooldown = 0.35;
808:   const target = findNearestEnemy(150);
809:   const dir = target ? { x: target.x - p.x, y: target.y - p.y } : p.facing;
810:   const len = Math.hypot(dir.x, dir.y) || 1;
811:   const vx = (dir.x / len) * 320;
812:   const vy = (dir.y / len) * 320;
813:   state.projectiles.push({
814:     x: p.x,
815:     y: p.y,
816:     vx,
817:     vy,
818:     radius: 8,
819:     damage: p.attackDamage || 18,
820:     color: '#f9d894',
821:     life: 0.7,
822:     from: 'player'
823:   });
824:   if (target) {
825:     target.hp -= (p.attackDamage || 18) * 0.9;
826:     logMessage(`${p.className} golpea: ${target.name}`, 'warn');
827:   }
828:   p.stamina = Math.max(0, p.stamina - 5);
829:   syncHud();

846: function findNearestEnemy(range = 200) {
847:   let nearest = null;
848:   let nearestDistance = Infinity;
849:   for (const enemy of state.enemies) {
850:     const d = dist(enemy, state.player);
851:     if (d < range && d < nearestDistance) {
852:       nearest = enemy;
853:       nearestDistance = d;
854:     }
855:   }
856:   return nearest;
857: }

859: function updatePlayer(dt) {
860:   const p = state.player;
861:   if (!p) return;
862: 
863:   p.attackCooldown = Math.max(0, p.attackCooldown - dt);
864:   p.dodgeCooldown = Math.max(0, p.dodgeCooldown - dt);
865:   p.invulnerable = Math.max(0, p.invulnerable - dt);
866:   p.satiety = Math.max(0, p.satiety - dt * 0.9);
867: 
868:   if (p.satiety <= 0) {
869:     p.hp -= dt * 7;
870:     if (p.hp <= 0) die();
871:   }
872: 
873:   const moveX = state.input.x;
874:   const moveY = state.input.y;
875:   const len = Math.hypot(moveX, moveY) || 1;
876:   const nx = moveX / len;
877:   const ny = moveY / len;
878: 
879:   if (Math.abs(moveX) > 0.05 || Math.abs(moveY) > 0.05) {
880:     p.facing.x = nx;
881:     p.facing.y = ny;
882:     const moveSpeed = p.speed * (0.7 + p.stamina / 140);
883:     p.x += nx * moveSpeed * dt;
884:     p.y += ny * moveSpeed * dt;
885:     p.stamina = Math.max(0, p.stamina - dt * 8);
886:   } else {
887:     p.stamina = Math.min(p.maxStamina, p.stamina + dt * 12);
888:   }
889: 
890:   p.x = clamp(p.x, 35, state.mapSize - 35);
891:   p.y = clamp(p.y, 35, state.mapSize - 35);
892:   state.camera.x = p.x;
893:   state.camera.y = p.y;
894:   ui.touchHint.classList.toggle('hidden', state.input.active);
895:   showCampAction();
896:   syncHud();
897: }

899: function updateProjectiles(dt) {
900:   for (const projectile of state.projectiles) {
901:     projectile.x += projectile.vx * dt;
902:     projectile.y += projectile.vy * dt;
903:     projectile.life -= dt;
904: 
905:     for (const enemy of state.enemies) {
906:       if (!enemy || projectile.from !== 'player') continue;
907:       if (dist(enemy, projectile) < enemy.radius + projectile.radius) {
908:         enemy.hp -= projectile.damage;
909:         projectile.life = 0;
910:         createBurst(projectile.x, projectile.y, '#fdd67b');
911:         break;
912:       }
913:     }
914:   }
915: 
916:   state.projectiles = state.projectiles.filter((proj) => proj.life > 0 && proj.x > 0 && proj.x < state.mapSize && proj.y > 0 && proj.y < state.mapSize);
917: }

919: function updateEnemies(dt) {
920:   for (const enemy of state.enemies) {
921:     if (!enemy) continue;
922:     const dx = state.player.x - enemy.x;
923:     const dy = state.player.y - enemy.y;
924:     const distToPlayer = Math.hypot(dx, dy) || 1;
925:     if (distToPlayer < 480) {
926:       enemy.x += (dx / distToPlayer) * enemy.speed * dt;
927:       enemy.y += (dy / distToPlayer) * enemy.speed * dt;
928:     }
929: 
930:     enemy.attackCooldown = Math.max(0, enemy.attackCooldown - dt);
931:     if (distToPlayer < enemy.radius + state.player.radius + 12 && enemy.attackCooldown <= 0) {
932:       const damage = Math.max(4, enemy.damage - (state.player.classId % 4));
933:       state.player.hp -= damage;
934:       state.player.invulnerable = 0.2;
935:       createBurst(state.player.x, state.player.y, '#ff7a7a');
936:       logMessage(`${enemy.name} te golpea por ${damage}.`, 'bad');
937:       enemy.attackCooldown = 0.8;
938:       if (state.player.hp <= 0) {
939:         die();
940:         return;
941:       }
942:     }
943: 
944:     if (enemy.hp <= 0) {
945:       state.player.xp += enemy.xp;
946:       state.player.gold += 4 + Math.floor(Math.random() * 6);
947:       createBurst(enemy.x, enemy.y, '#c9e57d');
948:       state.enemies = state.enemies.filter((item) => item !== enemy);
949:       if (Math.random() < 0.65) {
950:         state.loot.push({
951:           x: enemy.x,
952:           y: enemy.y,
953:           kind: enemy.lootDrop || 'madera',
954:           amount: 1,
955:           radius: 8,
956:           life: 14,
957:           color: RESOURCE_TYPES[enemy.lootDrop]?.color || '#a1d9ad'
958:         });
959:       }
960:       levelUpIfNeeded();
961:       logMessage(`${enemy.name} abatido.`, 'warn');
962:       break;
963:     }
964:   }
965: }

1007: function die() {
1008:   const p = state.player;
1009:   const xpLoss = Math.max(0, Math.floor(p.xp * 0.4));
1010:   const durabilityLoss = 14 + Math.random() * 16;
1011:   p.xp = Math.max(0, p.xp - xpLoss);
1012:   p.durability = Math.max(0, p.durability - durabilityLoss);
1013:   const corpseInventory = {};
1014:   for (const key of Object.keys(p.inventory)) {
1015:     const amount = p.inventory[key] || 0;
1016:     if (amount > 0 && Math.random() < 0.82) {
1017:       corpseInventory[key] = Math.max(1, Math.floor(amount * 0.8));
1018:       p.inventory[key] = Math.max(0, Math.floor(amount * 0.2));
1019:     }
1020:   }
1021:   state.corpse = {
1022:     x: p.x,
1023:     y: p.y,
1024:     title: 'Cadáver del Explorador',
1025:     loot: corpseInventory,
1026:     active: true,
1027:     radius: 26
1028:   };
1029:   p.hp = p.maxHp * 0.45;
1030:   p.mana = p.maxMana * 0.35;
1031:   p.stamina = p.maxStamina * 0.55;
1032:   p.x = state.map.camp.x + 30;
1033:   p.y = state.map.camp.y + 30;

1053: function render() {
1054:   const w = canvas.width;
1055:   const h = canvas.height;
1056:   ctx.clearRect(0, 0, w, h);
1057: 
1058:   const px = state.camera.x - w / 2;
1059:   const py = state.camera.y - h / 2;
1060: 
1061:   ctx.fillStyle = '#19251d';
1062:   ctx.fillRect(0, 0, w, h);
1063: 
1064:   ctx.save();
1065:   ctx.translate(-px, -py);
1066: 
1067:   const mapColor = state.map?.tier === 1 ? '#5e7d57' : state.map?.tier === 2 ? '#67775b' : state.map?.tier === 3 ? '#7a8da2' : state.map?.tier === 4 ? '#5d4f7e' : '#3d3d4a';
1068:   ctx.fillStyle = mapColor;
1069:   ctx.fillRect(0, 0, state.mapSize, state.mapSize);
1070: 
1071:   for (let x = 0; x <= state.mapSize; x += 120) {
1072:     ctx.strokeStyle = 'rgba(255,255,255,0.03)';
1073:     ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(x, 0); ctx.lineTo(x, state.mapSize); ctx.stroke();
1074:   }
1075:   for (let y = 0; y <= state.mapSize; y += 120) {
1076:     ctx.strokeStyle = 'rgba(255,255,255,0.03)';
1077:     ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(0, y); ctx.lineTo(state.mapSize, y); ctx.stroke();
1078:   }
1079: 
1080:   const camp = state.map?.camp || { x: 220, y: 220 };
1081:   ctx.fillStyle = '#d18d55';
1082:   ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(camp.x, camp.y, 44, 0, Math.PI * 2); ctx.fill();
1083:   ctx.fillStyle = '#f6d3a2';
1084:   ctx.fillRect(camp.x - 12, camp.y - 10, 24, 20);
1085: 
1086:   for (const node of state.resources) {
1087:     ctx.fillStyle = node.color;
1088:     ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(node.x, node.y, node.radius, 0, Math.PI * 2); ctx.fill();
1089:   }
1090: 
1091:   for (const enemy of state.enemies) {
1092:     ctx.fillStyle = enemy.color;
1093:     ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(enemy.x, enemy.y, enemy.radius, 0, Math.PI * 2); ctx.fill();
1094:     ctx.fillStyle = 'rgba(0,0,0,0.45)';
1095:     ctx.fillRect(enemy.x - 18, enemy.y - 26, 36, 4);
1096:     ctx.fillStyle = '#ef7d7d';
1097:     ctx.fillRect(enemy.x - 18, enemy.y - 26, 36 * (enemy.hp / enemy.maxHp), 4);
1098:   }
1099: 
1100:   for (const item of state.loot) {
1101:     ctx.fillStyle = item.color || '#d7c68f';
1102:     ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(item.x, item.y, item.radius, 0, Math.PI * 2); ctx.fill();
1103:   }
1104: 
1105:   if (state.corpse) {
1106:     ctx.fillStyle = '#8a8379';
1107:     ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(state.corpse.x, state.corpse.y, 16, 0, Math.PI * 2); ctx.fill();
1108:     ctx.fillStyle = '#d0cab1';
1109:     ctx.fillRect(state.corpse.x - 12, state.corpse.y + 10, 24, 10);
1110:   }
1111: 
1112:   for (const p of state.particles) {
1113:     ctx.fillStyle = p.color.replace(')', `, ${Math.max(0, p.alpha)})`).replace('hsl', 'hsla');
1114:     ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(p.x, p.y, p.radius, 0, Math.PI * 2); ctx.fill();
1115:   }
1116: 
1117:   const player = state.player;
1118:   if (player) {
1119:     ctx.fillStyle = '#d9e6f1';
1120:     ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(player.x, player.y, player.radius, 0, Math.PI * 2); ctx.fill();
1121:     ctx.fillStyle = '#f9da7a';
1122:     const aimX = player.x + player.facing.x * 18;
1123:     const aimY = player.y + player.facing.y * 18;
1124:     ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(player.x, player.y); ctx.lineTo(aimX, aimY); ctx.strokeStyle = '#f9da7a'; ctx.lineWidth = 3; ctx.stroke();
1125:   }
1126: 
1127:   for (const projectile of state.projectiles) {
1128:     ctx.fillStyle = projectile.color;
1129:     ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(projectile.x, projectile.y, projectile.radius, 0, Math.PI * 2); ctx.fill();
1130:   }
1131: 
1132:   ctx.restore();
1133: 
1134:   drawMinimap();
1135: }

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build and validate a playable, Android-friendly browser survival ARPG based on *Wild Frontier — La Frontera Maldita*.
- Compare the implementation with the GDD and report coverage, gaps, assumptions, and landscape/portrait guidance.

## Requirements
- Implement mobile-first gameplay with 15 maps, 90 enemies, 16 hybrid classes, gathering and crafting, survival systems, shelter, and corpse-run recovery.
- Preserve harsh progression and loss/recovery systems; briefly note assumptions when finished.

## Decisions
- Use a browser-based game shell.

## Work State
### Completed
- Preliminary game shell and systems exist; `xpFill` lookup and GDD-aligned gathering/crafting profession names were added.
- Confirmed definitions for 15 maps, 90 generated enemy entries, and 16 hybrid classes.
- Added `classIndex()` and `applyClassChoice()` in `js/main.js`; the helper validates level and IDs, preserves progress, applies primary-class bonuses once, and retains the chosen subclass when updating a class.

### Active
- Wire `renderClassSheet()` to `applyClassChoice()` and enforce primary/subclass unlock rules without replacing the player.
- Fix joystick pointer tracking and show the orientation prompt after viewport changes.
- Gate map access by player level/tier and reject invalid map indices.
- Implement meaningful crafting effects and correct recipe costs.
- Persist corpse state across saves/maps and make death inventory loss match the 80% non-bank loot rule.
- Validate gameplay, browser console, and screenshot; compare implementation against the GDD and report coverage, gaps, assumptions, and orientation guidance.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Connect class-sheet choices to `applyClassChoice()` and present class choices according to level and selection state.
2. Address map access, joystick/orientation, crafting, and corpse loss/persistence.
3. Run browser/gameplay checks and compare the result against the GDD.

## Relevant Files
- `js/main.js`: gameplay systems, maps/classes, save/load, controls, crafting, and corpse handling.
- `index.html`: HUD and game shell markup.
- `styles.css`: mobile-first layout and controls.
- `/tmp/gdd/01_GDD_MAESTRO_COMPLETO.md`: full design requirements and progression rules.
- `/tmp/gdd/04_GDD_DATA_STRUCTURES.json`: structured map and class definitions.

## Important Context
- Project files are uncommitted and untracked.
- `renderClassSheet()` still replaces the player on class selection; `applyClassChoice()` exists but is not connected.
- `createMap()` wraps indices and clears `state.corpse`; `loadGame()` recreates the map without restoring corpse state; `renderMapSheet()` currently allows every map.
- Crafting has six recipes; only three have distinct effects, `Pechera de cuero` requires undefined `hilo`, and other recipes report generic success.
- Death randomly assigns inventory to the corpse despite the message claiming 80% of non-bank loot is stored.
- Joystick handling relies on `:active` and element-level release/leave events; the orientation prompt is only checked during initial setup.
- GDD specifies class selection at levels 15 and 30 and says the corpse holds 80% of inventory at the death location; the bank protects stored materials and gold.
- Local server previously returned HTTP 200 at `http://127.0.0.1:8765`; Chromium is available, but Playwright and Puppeteer are not.

## Objective
- Build and validate a playable, Android-friendly browser survival ARPG based on *Wild Frontier — La Frontera Maldita*.
- Compare implementation with the GDD and report coverage, gaps, assumptions, and landscape/portrait guidance.

## Requirements
- Implement mobile-first gameplay with 15 maps, 90 enemies, 16 hybrid classes, gathering and crafting, survival systems, shelter, and corpse-run recovery.
- Preserve harsh progression and loss/recovery systems; briefly note assumptions when finished.

## Decisions
- Use a browser-based game shell.

## Work State
### Completed
- Preliminary game shell and systems exist; `xpFill` lookup and GDD-aligned gathering/crafting profession names were added.
- Confirmed definitions for 15 maps, 90 generated enemy entries, and 16 hybrid classes.
- Added `classIndex()` and `applyClassChoice()` in `js/main.js`; the helper validates level and IDs, preserves progress, applies primary-class bonuses once, and retains the chosen subclass when updating a class.
- Inspected relevant implementation for class selection, maps, crafting, corpse handling, joystick, and orientation.

### Active
- Wire `renderClassSheet()` to `applyClassChoice()` and enforce primary/subclass unlock rules without replacing the player.
- Fix joystick pointer tracking and show the orientation prompt after viewport changes.
- Gate map access by player level/tier and reject invalid map indices.
- Implement meaningful crafting effects and correct recipe costs.
- Persist corpse state across saves/maps and make death inventory loss match the 80% non-bank loot rule.
- Validate gameplay, browser console, and screenshot; compare implementation against the GDD and report coverage, gaps, assumptions, and orientation guidance.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Connect class-sheet choices to `applyClassChoice()` and present class choices according to level and selection state.
2. Address map access, joystick/orientation, crafting, and corpse loss/persistence.
3. Run browser/gameplay checks and compare the result against the GDD.

## Relevant Files
- `js/main.js`: gameplay systems, maps/classes, save/load, controls, crafting, and corpse handling.
- `index.html`: HUD and game shell markup.
- `styles.css`: mobile-first layout and controls.
- `/tmp/gdd/01_GDD_MAESTRO_COMPLETO.md`: full design requirements and progression rules.
- `/tmp/gdd/04_GDD_DATA_STRUCTURES.json`: structured map and class definitions.

## Important Context
- Project files are uncommitted and untracked.
- `renderClassSheet()` still replaces the player on class selection; `applyClassChoice()` exists but is not connected.
- `createMap()` wraps indices and clears `state.corpse`; `loadGame()` recreates the map without restoring corpse state; `renderMapSheet()` currently allows every map.
- Crafting has six recipes; only three have distinct effects, `Pechera de cuero` requires undefined `hilo`, and other recipes report generic success.
- Death randomly assigns inventory to the corpse despite the message claiming 80% of non-bank loot is stored.
- Joystick handling relies on `:active` and element-level release/leave events; the orientation prompt is only checked during initial setup.
- GDD specifies class selection at levels 15 and 30 and says the corpse holds 80% of inventory at the death location; the bank protects stored materials and gold.
- Local server previously returned HTTP 200 at `http://127.0.0.1:8765`; Chromium is available, but Playwright and Puppeteer are not.

1: # GAME DESIGN DOCUMENT (GDD) MAESTRO Y EXTENSO
2: ## PROJECT: WILD FRONTIER — LA FRONTERA MALDITA
3: 
4: - **Género:** ARPG de Supervivencia 2D / Sandbox de Exploración, Crafteo y Progresión Hardcore.
5: - **Plataforma:** Android (Optimizado para pantallas táctiles, HUD minimalista, rendimiento fluido en motores 2D como Godot 4 o Unity URP).
6: - **Enfoque de Diseño:** Dificultad implacable, progresión lenta y deliberada, interdependencia estricta de sistemas logísticos, economía restrictiva y castigos severos por muerte con opción de redención táctica (Corpse Run).
7: 
8: ---
9: 
10: ## 1. FILOSOFÍA DE DISEÑO Y PROGRESIÓN DURA
11: - **La Regla de Oro:** La habilidad mecánica de combate no basta; la inteligencia logística y la preparación previa son obligatorias. Los enemigos escalan con una curva empinada y las estadísticas base del personaje se estancan rápido si no se mejora el equipo mediante crafteo.
12: - **Interdependencia Crítica:** Entrar a una mazmorra de Tier alto sin pociones de alquimia, sin equipo reparado al 100% o sin alimentos cocinados de larga duración garantiza la derrota.
13: - **Progresión Orgánica:** Subir de nivel otorga puntos de atributo base y acceso a clases (Nv. 15) y subclases (Nv. 30), pero el verdadero poder proviene del Tier del equipo, las runas de encantamiento y las mejoras del Refugio Personal.
14: 
15: ## 2. LORE, HISTORIA Y ESTRUCTURA DE CAMPAÑA ("LA FRONTERA MALDITA")
16: - **El Lore:** La Gran Flota de Expedición imperial naufragó en las costas de **Aethelgard**, un continente virgen corrompido por la *Niebla Cenicienta*. Cada muerte sin rescate de cadáver alimenta la maldición del entorno. Los supervivientes se agrupan en el bastión de **Puerto Ocaso**.
17: - **Estructura de Campaña por Actos:**
18:   - **Acto I (Tier 1 | Niveles 1-15):** Playas, Praderas y Bosques Bajos. Supervivencia básica, recolección inicial y construcción del refugio de troncos.
19:   - **Acto II (Tier 2 | Niveles 16-30):** Pantanos Ácidos, Cañones y Ruinas Superiores. Elección de Clase Primaria y Subclase. Exigencia de alquimia defensiva.
20:   - **Acto III (Tier 3 | Niveles 31-45):** Tundra Eterna, Desierto Volcánico y Jungla Umbría. Clima extremo letal y recolección especializada.
21:   - **Acto IV (Tiers 4-5 | Niveles 46-60):** El Abismo Corrompido y el Núcleo de los Arquitectos hasta la Cámara del Eclipse.
22: 
23: ## 3. ARQUITECTURA DEL MUNDO: 15 MAPAS EXTENSOS (3 POR TIER)
24: Los mapas utilizan generación procedural por chunks para su distribución interna, manteniendo fija su identidad de bioma híbrida (sprites PNG artesanales + iluminación y clima por shaders):
25: 
26: ### Mapa 1.1: Playas del Náufrago (Tier 1: La Frontera Primitiva (Nv. 1-15))
27: - **Peligro Ambiental:** Mareas y emboscadas costeras
28: - **Ecología / Enemigos:** Cangrejos acorazados, bandidos novatos, slimes comunes
29: - **Recursos Clave:** Madera a la deriva, cobre superficial, peces costeros
30: 
31: ### Mapa 1.2: Praderas Susurrantes (Tier 1: La Frontera Primitiva (Nv. 1-15))
32: - **Peligro Ambiental:** Vientos dinámicos y manadas rápidas
33: - **Ecología / Enemigos:** Lobos grises, gobli-recolectores, jabalíes salvajes
34: - **Recursos Clave:** Hierbas curativas, lino silvestre, hierro bajo
35: 
36: ### Mapa 1.3: Bosques Bajos de la Niebla (Tier 1: La Frontera Primitiva (Nv. 1-15))
37: - **Peligro Ambiental:** Niebla matutina que reduce visibilidad
38: - **Ecología / Enemigos:** Arañas cazadoras, bandidos exploradores, treants jóvenes
39: - **Recursos Clave:** Roble denso, setas nocturnas, pieles medianas
40: 
41: ### Mapa 2.1: Pantanos Ácidos de Miasma (Tier 2: Tierras Interiores Hostiles (Nv. 16-30))
42: - **Peligro Ambiental:** Gas tóxico y lodo ralentizador
43: - **Ecología / Enemigos:** Slime de Ácido, sanguijuelas gigantes, hombres lagarto

## Objective
- Build and validate a playable, Android-friendly browser survival ARPG based on *Wild Frontier — La Frontera Maldita*.
- Compare the implementation with the GDD and report coverage, gaps, assumptions, and landscape/portrait guidance.

## Requirements
- Implement mobile-first gameplay with 15 maps, 90 enemies, 16 hybrid classes, gathering and crafting, survival systems, shelter, and corpse-run recovery.
- Preserve harsh progression and loss/recovery systems; briefly note assumptions when finished.

## Decisions
- Use a browser-based game shell.

## Work State

### Completed
- Preliminary game shell and systems exist; `xpFill` lookup and GDD-aligned gathering/crafting profession names were added.
- Confirmed definitions for 15 maps, 90 generated enemy entries, and 16 hybrid classes.
- Added `classIndex()` and `applyClassChoice()` in `js/main.js`; helper validates level and IDs, preserves progress, applies primary-class bonuses once, and retains the chosen subclass when updating a class.
- Inspected class selection, maps, crafting, corpse handling, joystick, and orientation implementation.
- Compared key requirements with `/tmp/gdd/01_GDD_MAESTRO_COMPLETO.md`; confirmed class unlock levels 15/30 and corpse recovery of 80% of inventory at death location.

### Active
- Wire `renderClassSheet()` to `applyClassChoice()` and enforce primary/subclass unlock rules without replacing the player.
- Fix joystick pointer tracking and show the orientation prompt after viewport changes.
- Gate map access by player level/tier and reject invalid map indices.
- Implement meaningful crafting effects and correct recipe costs.
- Persist corpse state across saves/maps and make death inventory loss match the 80% non-bank loot rule.
- Validate gameplay, browser console, and screenshot; compare implementation against the GDD and report coverage, gaps, assumptions, and orientation guidance.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Connect class-sheet choices to `applyClassChoice()` and present class choices according to level and selection state.
2. Address map access, joystick/orientation, crafting, and corpse loss/persistence.
3. Run browser/gameplay checks and compare the result against the GDD.

## Relevant Files
- `js/main.js`: gameplay systems, maps/classes, save/load, controls, crafting, and corpse handling.
- `index.html`: HUD and game shell markup.
- `styles.css`: mobile-first layout and controls.
- `/tmp/gdd/01_GDD_MAESTRO_COMPLETO.md`: full design requirements and progression rules.
- `/tmp/gdd/04_GDD_DATA_STRUCTURES.json`: structured map and class definitions.

## Important Context
- Project files are uncommitted and untracked.
- `renderClassSheet()` still replaces the player on class selection; `applyClassChoice()` exists but is not connected.
- `createMap()` wraps indices and clears `state.corpse`; `loadGame()` recreates the map without restoring corpse state; `renderMapSheet()` currently allows every map.
- Crafting has six recipes; only three have distinct effects, `Pechera de cuero` requires undefined `hilo`, and other recipes report generic success.
- Death randomly assigns inventory to the corpse despite the message claiming 80% of non-bank loot is stored.
- Joystick handling relies on `:active` and element-level release/leave events; the orientation prompt is only checked during initial setup.
- GDD specifies class selection at levels 15 and 30 and says the corpse holds 80% of inventory at the death location; the bank protects stored materials and gold.
- Local server previously returned HTTP 200 at `http://127.0.0.1:8765`; Chromium is available, but Playwright and Puppeteer are not.

## Objective
- Build and validate a playable, Android-friendly browser survival ARPG based on *Wild Frontier — La Frontera Maldita*.
- Compare implementation coverage with the GDD and report gaps, assumptions, and landscape/portrait guidance.

## Requirements
- Implement mobile-first gameplay with 15 maps, 90 enemies, 16 hybrid classes, gathering and crafting, survival systems, shelter, and corpse-run recovery.
- Preserve harsh progression and loss/recovery systems; briefly note assumptions when finished.

## Decisions
- Use a browser-based game shell.

## Work State

### Completed
- Preliminary game shell and systems exist; `xpFill` lookup and GDD-aligned gathering/crafting profession names were added.
- Confirmed definitions for 15 maps, 90 generated enemy entries, and 16 hybrid classes.
- Added `classIndex()` and `applyClassChoice()` in `js/main.js`, but class-sheet selection still bypasses them.
- Inspected class selection, maps, crafting, corpse handling, joystick, and orientation implementation.

### Active
- Wire `renderClassSheet()` to `applyClassChoice()` and enforce primary/subclass unlock rules at levels 15/30 without replacing the player.
- Fix joystick pointer tracking and show the orientation prompt after viewport changes.
- Gate map access by player level/tier and reject invalid map indices.
- Implement meaningful crafting effects and correct recipe costs.
- Persist corpse state across saves/maps and make death inventory loss match the 80% non-bank loot rule.
- Validate gameplay, browser console, and screenshot; compare implementation against the GDD and report coverage, gaps, assumptions, and orientation guidance.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Connect class-sheet choices to `applyClassChoice()` and present class choices according to level and selection state.
2. Address map access, joystick/orientation, crafting, and corpse loss/persistence.
3. Run browser/gameplay checks and compare the result against the GDD.

## Relevant Files
- `js/main.js`: gameplay systems, maps/classes, save/load, controls, crafting, and corpse handling.
- `index.html`: HUD and game shell markup.
- `styles.css`: mobile-first layout and controls.
- `/tmp/gdd/01_GDD_MAESTRO_COMPLETO.md`: full design requirements and progression rules.
- `/tmp/gdd/04_GDD_DATA_STRUCTURES.json`: structured map and class definitions.

## Important Context
- Project files are uncommitted and untracked.
- `renderClassSheet()` still replaces the player on class selection; `applyClassChoice()` exists but is not connected.
- `createMap()` wraps indices and clears `state.corpse`; `loadGame()` recreates the map without restoring corpse state; `renderMapSheet()` currently allows every map.
- Crafting has six recipes; only three have distinct effects, `Pechera de cuero` requires undefined `hilo`, and other recipes report generic success.
- Death randomly assigns inventory to the corpse despite the message claiming 80% of non-bank loot is stored.
- Joystick handling relies on `:active` and element-level release/leave events; the orientation prompt is only checked during initial setup.
- GDD specifies class selection at levels 15 and 30 and corpse recovery of 80% of inventory at the death location; the bank protects stored materials and gold.
- Local server previously returned HTTP 200 at `http://127.0.0.1:8765`; Chromium is available, but Playwright and Puppeteer are not.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build and validate a playable, Android-friendly browser survival ARPG based on *Wild Frontier — La Frontera Maldita*.
- Compare implementation coverage with the GDD and report gaps, assumptions, and landscape/portrait guidance.

## Requirements
- Implement mobile-first gameplay with 15 maps, 90 enemies, 16 hybrid classes, gathering and crafting, survival systems, shelter, and corpse-run recovery.
- Preserve harsh progression and loss/recovery systems; briefly note assumptions when finished.

## Decisions
- Use a browser-based game shell.

## Work State

### Completed
- Preliminary game shell and systems exist; `xpFill` lookup and GDD-aligned gathering/crafting profession names were added.
- Confirmed definitions for 15 maps, 90 generated enemy entries, and 16 hybrid classes.
- Added class-sheet progression UI that offers primary classes at level 15 and subclasses at level 30, uses `applyClassChoice()`, and no longer replaces the player.
- Added `mapRequiredLevel()` and `canEnterMap()` helpers for tier-based map gating (not yet connected to map selection).

### Active
- Wire map selection to `canEnterMap()`, reject invalid indices in `createMap()`, and keep inaccessible maps disabled.
- Fix joystick pointer tracking and show the orientation prompt after viewport changes.
- Implement meaningful crafting effects and correct recipe costs.
- Persist corpse state across saves/maps and make death inventory loss match the 80% non-bank loot rule.
- Validate gameplay, browser console, and screenshot; compare implementation against the GDD.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Finish map gating by connecting `canEnterMap()` to `renderMapSheet()` and validating indices in `createMap()`.
2. Complete corpse behavior: the save now includes corpse data and map changes no longer clear it, but map visibility, reliable 80% loss, recovery, and validation still need finishing.
3. Address crafting, joystick, and orientation issues.
4. Run browser/gameplay checks and report GDD coverage, gaps, assumptions, and orientation guidance.

## Relevant Files
- `js/main.js`: gameplay systems, maps/classes, save/load, controls, crafting, and corpse handling.
- `index.html`: HUD and game shell markup.
- `styles.css`: mobile-first layout and controls.
- `/tmp/gdd/01_GDD_MAESTRO_COMPLETO.md`: full design requirements and progression rules.
- `/tmp/gdd/04_GDD_DATA_STRUCTURES.json`: structured map and class definitions.

## Important Context
- Project files are uncommitted and untracked; recent edits are also uncommitted.
- `applyClassChoice()` is now connected to class selection; primary-class choice is permanent, and subclass selection is available at level 30.
- `canEnterMap()` requires tier levels 1, 16, 31, 46, and 56; map UI currently still lists all maps as selectable.
- `createMap()` no longer clears the corpse; save data now includes `corpse`, and `loadGame()` restores it. Corpse map visibility is toggled by `createMap()`, but rendering/recovery is not yet restricted to that map.
- Death still randomly transfers inventory and does not protect banked materials as claimed; GDD requires 80% of non-bank inventory recoverable at death location.
- Crafting has six recipes; only three have distinct effects, `Pechera de cuero` requires undefined `hilo`, and other recipes report generic success.
- Joystick handling relies on `:active` and element-level release/leave events; the orientation prompt is only checked during initial setup.
- GDD specifies class selection at levels 15 and 30 and corpse recovery of 80% of inventory at the death location; the bank protects stored materials and gold.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build and validate a playable, Android-friendly browser survival ARPG based on *Wild Frontier — La Frontera Maldita*.
- Compare implementation coverage with the GDD and report gaps, assumptions, and landscape/portrait guidance.

## Requirements
- Implement mobile-first gameplay with 15 maps, 90 enemies, 16 hybrid classes, gathering and crafting, survival systems, shelter, and corpse-run recovery.
- Preserve harsh progression and loss/recovery systems; briefly note assumptions when finished.

## Decisions
- Use a browser-based game shell.

## Work State

### Completed
- Added class-sheet progression for primary class selection at level 15 and subclass selection at level 30; choices use `applyClassChoice()` without replacing the player.
- Added `mapRequiredLevel()` and `canEnterMap()` helpers with tier gates at levels 1, 16, 31, 46, and 56.
- Added corpse data to save files, restore it during load, and preserve corpse state across map generation.
- Added map-index validation to `createMap()`; invalid or inaccessible indices now return `false`.

### Active
- Wire `canEnterMap()` into `renderMapSheet()`; disable inaccessible maps and handle rejected selections.
- Finish corpse behavior: add `mapIndex` on death, restrict visibility and recovery to the death map, enforce reliable 80% non-bank inventory loss, and validate recovery.
- Give all crafting recipes distinct effects and correct costs; resolve undefined `hilo` and item-key mismatches.
- Fix joystick pointer tracking and show the orientation prompt after viewport changes.
- Validate gameplay, browser console, and screenshot; compare implementation against the GDD.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Connect map eligibility checks to the map list and selection handler.
2. Complete corpse map ownership, visibility, loss, and recovery behavior.
3. Correct recipe costs and implement meaningful crafting effects.
4. Repair pointer-based joystick input and orientation prompt updates.
5. Run gameplay/browser validation and report GDD coverage, gaps, assumptions, and orientation guidance.

## Relevant Files
- `js/main.js`: gameplay systems, map/class progression, saving, crafting, corpse handling, and controls.
- `index.html`: game shell and HUD markup.
- `styles.css`: mobile-first layout and controls.
- `/tmp/gdd/01_GDD_MAESTRO_COMPLETO.md`: full design requirements and progression rules.
- `/tmp/gdd/04_GDD_DATA_STRUCTURES.json`: structured map and class definitions.

## Important Context
- Project files and recent edits are uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- `renderMapSheet()` still lists all maps as selectable, and its handler does not check `canEnterMap()`.
- `createMap()` now rejects invalid or gated indices but callers do not handle its `false` return.
- Corpse visibility toggling exists in `createMap()`, but corpse data currently lacks a `mapIndex`; rendering and recovery are not restricted by map.
- `die()` still randomly transfers inventory and does not protect banked materials; GDD calls for 80% of non-bank inventory recoverable at the death location.
- Crafting has six recipes; only three have distinct effects, `Pechera de cuero` requires undefined `hilo`, and other recipes report generic success.
- Joystick handling relies on `:active` and element-level release/leave events; the orientation prompt is only checked during initial setup.
- GDD specifies class selection at levels 15 and 30 and corpse recovery of 80% of inventory at the death location; the bank protects stored materials and gold.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build and validate a playable, Android-friendly browser survival ARPG based on *Wild Frontier — La Frontera Maldita*.
- Compare implementation coverage with the GDD and report gaps, assumptions, and landscape/portrait guidance.

## Requirements
- Implement mobile-first gameplay with 15 maps, 90 enemies, 16 hybrid classes, gathering and crafting, survival systems, shelter, and corpse-run recovery.
- Preserve harsh progression and loss/recovery systems; briefly note assumptions when finished.

## Decisions
- Use a browser-based game shell.

## Work State

### Completed
- Added class-sheet progression for primary class selection at level 15 and subclass selection at level 30.
- Added map-level gates through `mapRequiredLevel()` and `canEnterMap()`; `createMap()` rejects invalid or gated map indices.
- Added corpse persistence to saves and restore-on-load.
- Made crafting recipes distinct: corrected unavailable material costs and added effects for all six recipes, including weapon damage, armor, food, shelter, and rune upgrades.
- Updated the map sheet to disable locked maps and display their required levels.

### Active
- Complete map selection handling for rejected/inaccessible map indices.
- Finish corpse behavior: add death `mapIndex`, restrict rendering/recovery to the death map, enforce reliable 80% non-bank inventory loss, and validate recovery.
- Fix pointer-tracked joystick input and orientation prompt updates after viewport changes.
- Validate gameplay, browser console, and screenshot; compare implementation against the GDD and report coverage, gaps, assumptions, and orientation guidance.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add a guard and user feedback to map selection; handle `createMap()` returning `false`.
2. Complete corpse map ownership, inventory loss, visibility, and recovery rules.
3. Repair joystick pointer tracking and orientation prompt behavior on resize/orientation changes.
4. Run gameplay and browser checks, then report GDD coverage, gaps, assumptions, and orientation recommendations.

## Relevant Files
- `js/main.js`: gameplay systems, map/class progression, crafting, saving, corpse handling, and controls.
- `index.html`: game shell and HUD markup.
- `styles.css`: mobile-first layout and controls.
- `/tmp/gdd/01_GDD_MAESTRO_COMPLETO.md`: full design requirements and progression rules.
- `/tmp/gdd/04_GDD_DATA_STRUCTURES.json`: structured map and class definitions.

## Important Context
- Project files and edits are uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- Map buttons are disabled when locked, but the click handler still does not check `canEnterMap()` or handle `createMap()` failure.
- Corpse visibility toggling exists in `createMap()`, but corpse data still lacks a `mapIndex`; rendering and recovery are not restricted by map.
- `die()` still randomly transfers inventory and does not protect banked materials; GDD calls for 80% of non-bank inventory recoverable at the death location.
- Joystick handling still relies on `:active` and element-level release/leave events; the orientation prompt is only checked during initial setup.
- GDD specifies class selection at levels 15 and 30 and corpse recovery of 80% of inventory at the death location; the bank protects stored materials and gold.

2: ## PROJECT: WILD FRONTIER — LA FRONTERA MALDITA
3: 
4: - **Género:** ARPG de Supervivencia 2D / Sandbox de Exploración, Crafteo y Progresión Hardcore.
5: - **Plataforma:** Android (Optimizado para pantallas táctiles, HUD minimalista, rendimiento fluido en motores 2D como Godot 4 o Unity URP).
6: - **Enfoque de Diseño:** Dificultad implacable, progresión lenta y deliberada, interdependencia estricta de sistemas logísticos, economía restrictiva y castigos severos por muerte con opción de redención táctica (Corpse Run).
7: 
8: ---
9: 
10: ## 1. FILOSOFÍA DE DISEÑO Y PROGRESIÓN DURA
11: - **La Regla de Oro:** La habilidad mecánica de combate no basta; la inteligencia logística y la preparación previa son obligatorias. Los enemigos escalan con una curva empinada y las estadísticas base del personaje se estancan rápido si no se mejora el equipo mediante crafteo.
12: - **Interdependencia Crítica:** Entrar a una mazmorra de Tier alto sin pociones de alquimia, sin equipo reparado al 100% o sin alimentos cocinados de larga duración garantiza la derrota.
13: - **Progresión Orgánica:** Subir de nivel otorga puntos de atributo base y acceso a clases (Nv. 15) y subclases (Nv. 30), pero el verdadero poder proviene del Tier del equipo, las runas de encantamiento y las mejoras del Refugio Personal.
14: 
15: ## 2. LORE, HISTORIA Y ESTRUCTURA DE CAMPAÑA ("LA FRONTERA MALDITA")
16: - **El Lore:** La Gran Flota de Expedición imperial naufragó en las costas de **Aethelgard**, un continente virgen corrompido por la *Niebla Cenicienta*. Cada muerte sin rescate de cadáver alimenta la maldición del entorno. Los supervivientes se agrupan en el bastión de **Puerto Ocaso**.
17: - **Estructura de Campaña por Actos:**
18:   - **Acto I (Tier 1 | Niveles 1-15):** Playas, Praderas y Bosques Bajos. Supervivencia básica, recolección inicial y construcción del refugio de troncos.
19:   - **Acto II (Tier 2 | Niveles 16-30):** Pantanos Ácidos, Cañones y Ruinas Superiores. Elección de Clase Primaria y Subclase. Exigencia de alquimia defensiva.
20:   - **Acto III (Tier 3 | Niveles 31-45):** Tundra Eterna, Desierto Volcánico y Jungla Umbría. Clima extremo letal y recolección especializada.
21:   - **Acto IV (Tiers 4-5 | Niveles 46-60):** El Abismo Corrompido y el Núcleo de los Arquitectos hasta la Cámara del Eclipse.
22: 
23: ## 3. ARQUITECTURA DEL MUNDO: 15 MAPAS EXTENSOS (3 POR TIER)
24: Los mapas utilizan generación procedural por chunks para su distribución interna, manteniendo fija su identidad de bioma híbrida (sprites PNG artesanales + iluminación y clima por shaders):
25: 
26: ### Mapa 1.1: Playas del Náufrago (Tier 1: La Frontera Primitiva (Nv. 1-15))
27: - **Peligro Ambiental:** Mareas y emboscadas costeras
28: - **Ecología / Enemigos:** Cangrejos acorazados, bandidos novatos, slimes comunes
29: - **Recursos Clave:** Madera a la deriva, cobre superficial, peces costeros
30: 
31: ### Mapa 1.2: Praderas Susurrantes (Tier 1: La Frontera Primitiva (Nv. 1-15))
32: - **Peligro Ambiental:** Vientos dinámicos y manadas rápidas
33: - **Ecología / Enemigos:** Lobos grises, gobli-recolectores, jabalíes salvajes
34: - **Recursos Clave:** Hierbas curativas, lino silvestre, hierro bajo
35: 
36: ### Mapa 1.3: Bosques Bajos de la Niebla (Tier 1: La Frontera Primitiva (Nv. 1-15))
37: - **Peligro Ambiental:** Niebla matutina que reduce visibilidad
38: - **Ecología / Enemigos:** Arañas cazadoras, bandidos exploradores, treants jóvenes
39: - **Recursos Clave:** Roble denso, setas nocturnas, pieles medianas
40: 
41: ### Mapa 2.1: Pantanos Ácidos de Miasma (Tier 2: Tierras Interiores Hostiles (Nv. 16-30))
42: - **Peligro Ambiental:** Gas tóxico y lodo ralentizador
43: - **Ecología / Enemigos:** Slime de Ácido, sanguijuelas gigantes, hombres lagarto
44: - **Recursos Clave:** Raíz de miasma, cuero ácido, estaño pantanoso
45: 
46: ### Mapa 2.2: Cañones de Piedra Quebrada (Tier 2: Tierras Interiores Hostiles (Nv. 16-30))
47: - **Peligro Ambiental:** Desprendimientos y puentes estrechos
48: - **Ecología / Enemigos:** Bandidos ballesteros, aves de presa rocosas, escorpiones de roca
49: - **Recursos Clave:** Hierro puro, carbón mineral, plumas de caza
